correctness.rationale: The proof is an exhaustive classification. For n>=5 the even member with Omega<=2 is 2r with r an odd prime. The odd neighbor is necessarily a prime, prime square, or product of two distinct odd primes. Totient equality plus consecutiveness gives contradictions in all three cases. The finite boundary n=2,3,4 leaves only n=3.

value.rationale: The Omega<=2 layer is the natural first nontrivial multiplicative stratum for a classical open consecutive-totient equation. The theorem gives a complete, unbounded structural barrier: every solution after n=3 must have at least three prime factors, counted with multiplicity, on one side. This is stronger in kind than bounded enumeration and supplies a reusable starting constraint for higher-layer analysis.
